chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who became junub, then performed ghusl before urinating, then later saw something. He said: He does not repeat the ghusl; that is not something for which he saw [i.e. requiring repetition].

So the proper way of reconciling these two reports is one of two things: the first is that the one washing had exerted effort to urinate but it did not become possible for him, and in that case repeating the ghusl was not obligatory upon him. The second is that this applies specifically to one who did that forgetfully. And what indicates that is what...

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ الْغُسْلَ: he does not repeat the ghusl
key_terms.يَبُولَ: to urinate, here as istibrāʾ before ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does a person have to repeat ghusl if discharge appears after ghusl done before urinating?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a junub person who performs ghusl before urinating and then notices some discharge afterward. It states that ghusl is not repeated in this case, and the closing explanation reconciles the reports by restricting it either to one who tried but was unable to urinate, or to one who acted forgetfully.
